theme.title: NBA Mix 58
theme.subtitle: Five moments from across NBA history
theme.recap: Five NBA stories, five different numbers: a quick tour of stars, teams, records and surprises.

questions.prompt: In the 1977 title clincher, how many rebounds did Bill Walton grab?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bill Walton's 20 points, 23 rebounds, 7 assists and 8 blocks kept the game in Portland's favor.

funFacts.text: Bill Walton was named Finals MVP after leading Portland to its first championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Walton was named finals MVP

funFacts.text: CBS cut away so quickly after the clincher that viewers missed the locker-room trophy presentation.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: CBS cut away from their NBA coverage very quickly after the game ended, skipping the trophy presentation

funFacts.text: Walton ended the game by batting a missed Philadelphia shot out toward midcourt as time expired.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bill Walton reached over all of them and slapped the ball up the court

questions.prompt: In 2018–19, James Harden scored 30 or more in how many straight games?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: his 30-point streak which started on December 13, all the way to a surprising 32 games until ending on February 25.

funFacts.text: An early-season altercation between Chris Paul and Rajon Rondo became part of a turbulent Rockets campaign.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including an on-court altercation between rival guards Chris Paul and Rajon Rondo

funFacts.text: Trevor Ariza's departure and injuries contributed to Houston's rough start before Harden carried the recovery.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: injuries among its players, and losing core players including Trevor Ariza

funFacts.text: The Rockets recovered enough to claim another postseason berth, extending their playoff-appearance run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they clinched another playoff spot for the 7th straight year

questions.prompt: Scottie Pippen tied the Finals record for threes in Game 3 of 1997. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Scottie Pippen tying a then-Finals record with seven 3-pointers

funFacts.text: Pippen's long-range clinic still came in a loss because Karl Malone dominated the interior for Utah.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Utah was led by Karl Malone, who scored 37 points and had 10 rebounds

funFacts.text: The Salt Lake City crowd was so loud that Bulls players covered their ears during the introductions.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls players plugged their ears, due to the loud cheers and fireworks

funFacts.text: Chicago nearly erased a big late deficit, but Utah earned its first win of the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chicago attempted a 4th-quarter comeback, cutting a 24-point deficit down to 7

questions.prompt: Chris "Birdman" Andersen shot what percentage from the field in the 2013 playoffs?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris "Birdman" Andersen shot 80.7 percent (46-of-57) from the field in the 2013 postseason

funFacts.text: Birdman arrived on a short ten-day contract in January rather than starting the year on Miami's roster.

funFacts.text: Birdman's nickname came from his wingspan and shot-blocking style, not from his colorful tattoos.
